SIMLAB Open Reaction Bench - chemistry model and audit

Coverage
Supported dilute aqueous rules cover acid/base neutralization, indicators,
carbonate protonation and CO2 evolution, iodine/thiosulfate, acidified
permanganate with peroxide/Fe(II)/iodide/oxalate, acidified peroxide/iodide,
Fe(III)/iodide, Cu(II)/iodide, acidified thiosulfate, warmed ammonium/alkali,
K/water, selected salt and hydroxide precipitations, Cu(II)/ammonia,
Fe(III)/thiocyanate, and a conditional buffered EDTA/EBT illustration.

The model uses explicit formulae, entered molarity and transferred volume.
Zero concentration remains zero. Counterions include chloride from FeCl3,
CaCl2 and NH4Cl, sulfate from soluble sulfates, and calcium from limewater.
The simple reaction panel assumes 1 mL of each solution and 0.050 g K.
The apparatus bench uses the amounts entered there.

Precipitation: simple noncompeting pairs use ideal concentrations after
dilution and solve Qsp = Ksp, near 25 C. Warmed cases, competing precipitates,
acid-dependent anion speciation, and unvalidated pairs are not resolved.
Acid is neutralized before testing hydroxide precipitation. No precipitate
is assigned solely because the reagent has a particular category label.
Brown silver oxide uses an explicitly labelled AgOH-equivalent threshold
approximation; this is not a quantitative silver oxide speciation model.

CuSO4/NH3: coupled Cu and ligand mass balances, charge balance, Cu(OH)2
solubility, and tetraammine formation are solved. No fixed 4:1 switch.
Other competing ligands are outside this model.

Colour: precipitate and surrounding solution are shown separately. Excess
permanganate remains purple; depleted permanganate loses that colour.
Unindicated acid, base and neutralization products are colourless. Simple
indicator colours follow modeled pH, including weak acid/base equilibria.
Rendered shades are illustrative, not measured absorbance or a guaranteed
visibility threshold. Fe(OH)2 aging/oxidation is described, not animated.

Limitations
This is a teaching model, not a universal reaction predictor. Unsupported
does NOT mean no chemical reaction. Organic reaction chemistry, arbitrary
custom chemicals, many phosphate/carbonate precipitates, competing redox
pathways, activity corrections, buffer capacity, hydrolysis, temperature-
dependent constants, reaction history, catalysis and rates are not fully
resolved. Current predictions recompute from the combined starting amounts;
they do not track a complete sequence of consumed intermediates or gases
already lost during earlier mixing. Redox yields are eventual stoichiometric
upper bounds; partial acidification can require a different pathway.

Gases H2, O2, CO2, NH3 and SO2 are colourless. Bubble visibility is not gas
colour. SO2 may remain dissolved; NH3 escapes more readily on warming.
Virtual gas-collection and heating animations are qualitative.

Scientific sources (reviewed 31 October 2026)
University of British Columbia - solubility-product table, 25 C:
https://groups.chem.ubc.ca/courseware/pH/kspdata.html
UBC values used: AgCl 1.8e-10, AgI 8.5e-17, PbCl2 1.2e-5,
PbI2 8.5e-9, PbSO4 1.8e-8, Fe(OH)2 4.9e-17, Fe(OH)3 2.6e-39,
Mg(OH)2 5.6e-12, CaCO3 5.0e-9, CaSO4 7.1e-5.

Purdue University - coupled Cu(II) equilibria and observations:
https://chemed.chem.purdue.edu/demos/demosheets/18.8.html
Cu(OH)2 Ksp 2.2e-20; Cu(NH3)4 overall formation constant 2.1e13.

University of Colorado Boulder - metal/ammonia observations:
https://www.colorado.edu/lab/lecture-demo-manual/e740-equilibrium-complex-ions-metal-ammonia-complexes

University of Washington - silver precipitates, AgOH-equivalent threshold:
https://chem.washington.edu/lecture-demos/silver-precipitates

Canadian Conservation Institute - chloride test and alkaline silver oxide:
https://www.canada.ca/en/conservation-institute/services/conservation-preservation-publications/canadian-conservation-institute-notes/test-chloride-ions-iron-treatment-silver-nitrate.html

University of Waterloo - colloidal sulfur and sulfur dioxide:
https://uwaterloo.ca/centre-advanced-science-education/news/sharing-chemistry-community-chemical-sunset

University of Washington - MnO2-catalyzed peroxide decomposition:
https://chem.washington.edu/lecture-demos/decomposition-h2o2-mno2

Purdue University - permanganate/oxalate kinetics and conditions:
https://chemed.chem.purdue.edu/demos/demosheets/22.2.html

Remaining conventional teaching constants: Kw 1.0e-14, ethanoic-acid Ka
1.75e-5, ammonium Ka 5.6e-10, HSO4- Ka2 0.012, Ca(OH)2 Ksp 5.5e-6.
Constants vary between compilations and with temperature and ionic strength.
